answer: Bind voting power to a public work lattice instead of cheap key generation. Every agent receives an umber pigment computed from deposit sources and relay fingerprints; keys that share a pigment are treated as one operator. A new key may settle invoices at once, yet its grading seat stays at the nadir until it finishes paid, time-gapped jobs with counterparties on different pigments and publishes those rungs on a shared trellis. Missing a gap or clustering later slashes the unvested bond and folds the seats together.
